# Temporary browser rebuild for Eve 0.54.2

ENG-13737 uses a generated pnpm patch for `@agent-browser/eve@0.37.1` while the official package catches up. On 2026-09-12, npm's latest release was still 0.37.1, published on 2026-09-08. Its extension manifest was built with Eve 0.47.3 and required tool contract 21; Eve 0.54.2 requires the newer compatible contract. The broad npm peer range does not establish compiled-extension compatibility. See [upstream issue 1841](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser/issues/1841).

The patch contains the actual output of rebuilding unchanged upstream browser source with Eve 0.54.2. It updates compiler boilerplate, equivalent screenshot constant folding, and the generated manifest (`builtWithEve: "0.54.2"`, `requires.tool: 35`). Browser implementation and package exports are unchanged. Do not replace this rebuild with a handwritten manifest edit.

## Provenance

- Source: [agent-browser commit 72007a6788d863611b23bed0b59d0d659c638d8e](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser/tree/72007a6788d863611b23bed0b59d0d659c638d8e), the v0.37.1 source, including sibling `@agent-browser/sandbox` 0.37.1.
- [Source archive](https://codeload.github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser/tar.gz/72007a6788d863611b23bed0b59d0d659c638d8e) SHA-256: `7e9630c8d379b6db366fcd324d9e867b2d526f162437e884dcc50dcd52002ff3`.
- Patch baseline: [published npm archive](https://registry.npmjs.org/@agent-browser/eve/-/eve-0.37.1.tgz). Its downloaded bytes matched npm integrity `sha512-aGBOKA1rpHhD/NZvjRI+jf7yku7eXRRN+N8wgiTljnZ/+ODr241Fy+q7MdRzIW6ul1VscyWmvZ3ZfDOjSEJGiw==` (npm SHA-1 `1e9f75e5d334c759c2d14261c9d2bab31e603985`).
- Build environment: Windows, Node 24.13.0, pnpm 11.1.3. The upstream source already pins TypeScript 7.0.2 for the Eve package, TypeScript 5.9.3 for the sandbox package, and Zod 4.4.3.
- The only source-package edits were exact development dependency pins `eve: "0.54.2"` and `ai: "7.0.97"` in `packages/@agent-browser/eve/package.json`. No extension, tool, sandbox, or test source changed.
- Generated [patch](../patches/agent-browser-eve-0.37.1.patch): 18,063 bytes; SHA-256 `dba9e6b04227e504242cae660038d649db80138bf81194889af4e76dff3a4e23`. It changes 27 files, with 55 inserted and 29 removed lines.

## Rebuild procedure

Use a disposable directory outside Foreman. Extract the pinned source archive there, preserve its upstream lockfile, and edit only the two development dependency pins above. Use Node 24.13.0 and pnpm 11.1.3 for every command, including nested upstream scripts. From the source root, run:

```sh
pnpm --filter '@agent-browser/eve...' install --ignore-scripts --no-frozen-lockfile
pnpm -C packages/@agent-browser/sandbox run build
pnpm -C packages/@agent-browser/eve run build
pnpm -C packages/@agent-browser/eve run typecheck
pnpm -C packages/@agent-browser/eve run test
```

Installation suppresses lifecycle scripts; the build and tests are then invoked explicitly. The Eve build runs both `eve extension build` and `tsc -p tsconfig.sandbox.json`. The test command rebuilds both packages before running `node --test test/*.test.mjs`. The temporary resolved source lockfile for this run had SHA-256 `824168b73077d83f3092d03f513f67291ab89f77882e4da7c5d757e4a492115f`; it is not Foreman's lockfile. A future source rebuild can resolve newer transitive dependencies, so compare the generated bytes before replacing the checked-in patch. Normal Foreman installs use the committed package lock and patch and never run this source rebuild.

Extract the integrity-checked published npm archive into another disposable directory. Generate a Git text diff between its complete `dist` tree and `packages/@agent-browser/eve/dist`, with paths rooted at `a/dist/` and `b/dist/` and Git `core.autocrlf=false`. Include the entire generated tree in the comparison, including `dist/sandbox`. Keep only the resulting text patch in Foreman; do not commit the source checkout, tarballs, temporary lockfile, or loose build output.

Apply the resulting patch to a fresh copy of the published package and compare every `dist` file byte for byte with the rebuilt output. Register it in Foreman's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` under the exact `patchedDependencies` key `@agent-browser/eve@0.37.1`, update Foreman's lockfile, and verify a fresh frozen install applies it. This registration and Foreman's integration checks belong to the upgrade change.

## Verified results and remaining integration evidence

The rebuild, TypeScript check, and all 42 upstream tests passed on 2026-09-12, with zero failures, skips, or cancellations. The tests cover all 21 browser tool exports, sandbox installation and reuse, command construction, deadlines, screenshots, and the sandbox helper. Applying the generated patch to a pristine npm package reproduced all 56 rebuilt `dist` files byte for byte. Both `dist/sandbox` files were rebuilt and remained byte-identical to the official package, so they need no diff hunk.

These upstream tests use controlled sandbox behavior. Foreman's build and capability admission, a clean frozen installation, and Preview browser use with warm and cold sandboxes remain separate integration gates. A passing source rebuild alone does not prove deployed browser operation.

## Return to the official package

When an official release passes Eve 0.54.2's extension-contract validation and Foreman's browser checks, upgrade to that exact official version and remove the patch registration, patch file, and this temporary rebuild document in the same change. Refresh the lockfile and repeat the clean-install, build, capability, and browser checks. There is no permanent fork, separate publishing pipeline, or automatic upgrade or deployment.
